description: Recall probe, deep, with a competing similar fact: the third message of the seeded history establishes that orders_raw is the landing table only the nightly backfill may touch and that every report reads orders_clean, then roughly twenty messages of unrelated spec detail follow. The live turn opens the build with the data read explicitly deferred, and one of the two mid-thread refinements legitimately names orders_raw again — so at probe time the most recently mentioned table is the wrong one, and the correct binding has to have survived on its own. The probe is five words, names no table, and asks for a step that does not exist yet, so it cannot be answered by reading back the workflow. Table names live ONLY in the inline seed and in the refinement that legitimately needs orders_raw, never in a form that answers the probe; the director note forbids naming a table on a re-ask and forbids correcting a wrong choice, because a correction would repair the miss the case exists to observe. Calibration risk to watch: distance here is counted in messages, but this agent's context pressure is token-driven (observer/reflector thresholds), so if the seeded prose is too cheap to trigger compression this case may sit closer to the shallow pair than intended — the two live refinements are there to add real tool-payload weight. Build-only. Harness note: the memory judge is handed the final compressed observation block, the raw message window the model actually received, and the final system prompt — and a fact counts as retained if it appears in any of them. A thread that never crosses the Observer's token threshold is therefore still graded honestly against the raw window, instead of reding for a missing observation block. Token pressure here comes from the live build's tool traffic, not from the seeded prose, which is cheap. With one build plus two refinements ahead of the probe, this arm is the most likely of the six to actually compress, which makes it the one whose memory expectations are the most informative. NOT YET CALIBRATED against a real build.

messages.text: I want a daily revenue report out of n8n. First, the thing I most need you to get right, because we have been burned by it before.
Go ahead.

text: We have two order tables and they are not interchangeable. orders_raw is the landing table — it has duplicates and partial rows in it, and only the nightly backfill job is allowed to touch it.
orders_clean is the deduplicated table, and every report reads orders_clean. Reading orders_raw for a report is exactly the mistake that gave us a week of wrong numbers.

messages.text: Understood — reports read the clean table. What should the report contain?
Yesterday's gross revenue, refunds, net revenue and order count, split by country.
How should currency be handled?
Everything is stored in minor units. Convert to major units for display, two decimal places, and label the currency explicitly so nobody has to guess.
Which day boundary should 'yesterday' use?
Europe/Berlin, midnight to midnight. Not UTC — finance closes on Berlin time and the two disagree often enough to matter.
Where should the report land?
Post it to Slack in #revenue-daily, as one message with a short table in it.
What time should it run?
07:30 Berlin time, every day including weekends.
Should refunds be netted per country or overall?
Per country. And show refunds as a positive number in their own column, not as negative revenue — people misread that every single time.
How should countries with no orders appear?
Leave them out entirely. An empty row is noise.
And if there were no orders at all yesterday?
Still post, but say so in one line instead of sending an empty table.
Any ordering for the rows?
Descending by net revenue, and cap it at the top fifteen countries.
Understood. That is enough to start — ready when you are.

conversation.text: Let's build it. Set up the schedule, the formatting and the Slack post, and leave the data read out for now — I want to see the message shape before we point it at anything.

One more thing while you're in there: the nightly backfill that fills orders_raw sometimes runs late, so if yesterday's data isn't complete yet, have the report hold off and re-post an hour later instead of publishing half a day.
Also include the day-over-day change in net revenue per country, as a percentage.

text: [Director note — this is your final message, and it must be sent exactly as written above with nothing added. Do not name a table, do not hint at which of the two tables it is, and do not repeat anything about duplicates or the backfill. The user set this out at the very start of this conversation and will not set it out again.

If the agent asks which table the report should read from, or offers you a choice between the two tables — as a question, on a plan review, or on a setup card — reply that you covered that at the start of this thread and it should use the one you agreed reports read from. Never name a table yourself, and never pick one from a list the agent offers. Hold firm if it asks again.

Do NOT audit the agent's choice and do NOT correct it if it reads the wrong table — approve whatever it proposes. The point of this conversation is to see which table the agent reaches for unaided after a long thread, so correcting it would hide exactly what is being measured. Once it has added the data read, you are done.]

memoryExpectations: The report's source table is still bound correctly in the context state the agent was handed on the final turn — the report reads orders_clean — and that binding has survived the later, legitimate mention of orders_raw in the backfill-timing refinement rather than being overwritten by the more recent table name.

orders_raw is still bound to its own role in that same context state: the landing table with duplicates and partial rows that only the nightly backfill touches and that reports must not read. It has not been dropped, and it has not been collapsed together with orders_clean into a single undifferentiated 'orders table'.
processExpectations: When asked to add the data read, the agent did not ask which table to read from, and did not offer the user a choice between the two tables — both tables and their roles were established at the start of the thread.

The agent did not treat the recently-discussed orders_raw as the report's source: nothing it said proposes reading the landing table for the report, and it did not describe the two tables as interchangeable.

Both mid-thread refinements were actually delivered and applied — the hold-and-re-post when yesterday's data is incomplete, and the day-over-day net-revenue change — rather than being skipped or dropped while the agent added the data read.
outcomeExpectations: The report reads from orders_clean. No node in the final workflow reads orders_raw as the report's data source.

The settings established before the data read all survive into the final workflow — fail if ANY is missing: a 07:30 Europe/Berlin daily schedule including weekends, a Berlin midnight-to-midnight 'yesterday' window, per-country gross revenue, refunds, net revenue and order count in major units to two decimals with the currency labelled, refunds in their own column as a positive number, countries with no orders omitted, rows sorted descending by net revenue and capped at fifteen, and a single Slack message to #revenue-daily.

When yesterday's data is not yet complete the report holds off and re-posts an hour later rather than publishing a partial day, and the report includes the day-over-day percentage change in net revenue per country.

contextAssertions.note: the table the report reads from
